The private Python producer writes headerless CSV rows and the Stata consumer renames positional variables and maps columns into topics. The admitted producer/consumer excerpts do not establish an exact conflicting column mapping; preserve this as an unresolved schema question, not a confirmed incompatibility.

Source 20 exports list_public.xls; source A reads list_public.xls.xlsx and consumes a website column, then writes results_public.csv. Source 23 separately consumes index_public.csv. The compatible case, path, format, and field mapping between these stages remains unresolved; these names are kept as distinct products pending a supported mapping.

Source 23 directly consumes index_private.csv, but the admitted direct evidence does not establish its producer, field schema, or relationship to the public index. The unresolved producer contract is retained without inferring absence or private-data content.

The nonfinancial source creates log_employees, keeps log_emp in an intermediate branch, and later keeps log_employees. The admitted static record does not establish which branch supplies the later field or the applicable variable-abbreviation context. Stata may resolve a unique variable-name abbreviation; this remains a field-lineage question, not a confirmed runtime break.

Eleven one-row native probes establish the listed column readability and separate joins, not full population, history, or all required years. COMPANY.weburl and DSENAMES.SHRCD remain separate inputs joined by their keys/effective dates.

Public CDX documentation and the packaged JSON examples do not establish complete firm-level snapshot coverage. Public analysis also consumes wb_full and wb_full_updated, whose producer and field/history handoff remain unverified in the admitted workflow.

A documented LM 2018 year directory is a positive discovery pointer. Source 6 consumes LM_10X_Summaries_2018.csv fields fye, form_type, n_words, n_unique_words, grossfilesize, and netfilesize; the exact local file schema/readability and required history remain unverified.

The datasheet identifies commercial data vendors and source code names distinct Orbis/Zephyr inputs. Local catalog misses do not establish that a dataset, license, or route is absent; exact authorized exports, fields, and vintages remain unverified.

The source consumes distinct 8kplumlee, dq_2017, NAICS, supply-chain, IOR/SC, list_gvkey_date, IBES-link, complexity, and segment products. determinant_reg is source-generated in the public-firm dataset stage and consumed downstream; it is not a separate raw acquisition. The other named inputs still lack complete local field/readability and historical-coverage proof.
